SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WASTE DISPOSALIN THE CLASSROOM
Subject: HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Waste disposalin the classroom helps you succeed in HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: WASTE DISPOSALIN THE CLASSROOM
Study Waste disposalin the classroom like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify containers used for (papers, pencil sharpening, 3.

What this means
In this part you learn to identify containers used for (papers, pencil sharpening, 3.. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify containers used for (papers, pencil sharpening, 3..
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Waste disposalin the classroom” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify containers used for (papers, pencil sharpening, 3.. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Waste disposalin the classroom is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Waste disposalin the classroom” around your school. (skill: identify containers used for (papers, pencil sharpening, 3.)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Waste disposalin the classroom to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify containers used for (papers, pencil sharpening, 3..
3. Make one local Kenya example of Waste disposalin the classroom from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Waste disposalin the classroom: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Waste disposalin the classroom?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What waste is found in classroom the learner should be able to: identify the various types of the classroom?
2. Where do we put waste found in the classroom, using realia or pictures in the classroom?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Waste disposalin the classroom means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify containers used for (papers, pencil sharpening, 3..

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
